1995.kid: The mobile company’s telephone exchange. For a computer’s call it has a rack of modems: one of them takes your laptop’s data and beeps it on into the ordinary phone network, like the modem on a computer at home.
1995.nerd: The mobile switching centre (MSC) with its interworking function (IWF, GSM 09.07): the IWF ends RLP and plays the bytes as a V.32 modem at 9.6 kbit/s into a 64 kbit/s PCM slot towards the PSTN (or, to an ISDN number, sends them digital, rate-adapted by V.110). Still no IP: PPP rides inside the modem tones.

peek.kid: The switch doesn’t open your parcel. Its modem turns the laptop’s data into beeps and sends them on down the phone line.
peek.nerd: The IWF strips RLP and remodulates the byte stream as V.32; the PPP frames inside are carried, not read.
